sections.label: Water demand growth since Independence
sections.summary: Water demand has grown more than six times since Independence to meet population and economy needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Water demand has grown by more than six times since Independence to meet the needs of a growing population and the economy.

sections.label: New desalination plants built
sections.summary: New desalination plants were built in Tuas, Marina East and Jurong Island, bringing the total to five.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Since then, we have built new desalination plants in Tuas, Marina East and Jurong Island, bringing the total to five desalination plants today.

sections.label: Singapore daily water consumption
sections.summary: Singapore consumes about 440 mgd, expected to almost double by 2065, with the non-domestic sector driving growth.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Singapore currently consumes about 440 million gallons of water per day (mgd), which is equivalent to about 800 Olympic-sized swimming pools.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Our consumption is expected to almost double by 2065, with the non-domestic sector being the major source of demand growth.

sections.label: 3Rs and Public Utilities Act update
sections.summary: The Bill updates the Public Utilities Act 2001 on recycling requirements for large water users and charges on large private water suppliers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: By adopting the 3Rs concept – reduce, reuse and recycle – which we are all familiar with, we can conserve water and use it more efficiently, making every single drop of water count.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: This Bill serves to update the Public Utilities Act 2001 (PUA) in two main areas: recycling requirements for large water users and to impose charges on large private water suppliers (PWS).

sections.label: Recycling rate for wafer fabrication
sections.summary: New wafer fabrication plants in front-end semiconductor manufacturing must meet a minimum 50% recycling rate.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: For new wafer fabrication plants involved in front-end semiconductor manufacturing, we will require a minimum 50% recycling rate.

sections.label: Recycling specified waste streams
sections.summary: Companies with more limited recycled water use cases must recycle specified waste streams instead of meeting a minimum recycling rate.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Their use cases for recycled water are more limited, compared to those involved in wafer fabrication.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Hence, instead of requiring a minimum recycling rate, we will require the recycling of specified waste streams for these companies.

sections.label: Water recycling requirements for new projects
sections.summary: Requirements will apply from January 2024 to new projects, including expansions consuming at least 60,000 cubic metres of water annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: This allowed them to achieve industry-leading recycling rates of over 75%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: We intend for the requirements to apply from January 2024 to new projects, including the expansion of existing plants that will consume at least 60,000 cubic metres of water annually.

sections.label: Payback periods for recycling infrastructure
sections.summary: Payback for recycling infrastructure is typically two to four years for wafer fabrication and under one year for electronics and biomedical industries.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: The payback period for the recycling infrastructure is assessed to be typically between two and four years for wafer fabrication companies and less than one year for the electronics and biomedical industries.

sections.label: Raised funding caps and WEF extension
sections.summary: Funding caps for WEF and IWSDF were raised to $5 million each, and PUB will make WEF funding available until end-2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Since July 2023, we have raised the funding caps for WEF and IWSDF from $1 million and $4 million respectively, to $5 million each for each project.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: As such, PUB will extend its support to companies by making WEF funding available to eligible companies until end-2025 to help raise their recycling rates to the mandatory levels.

sections.label: Projected payback periods with funds
sections.summary: PUB projects that plants recycling at higher rates using the funds can reduce payback periods to about five years or less.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Based on PUB’s projections, plants recycling at higher rates, which tap on the funds, can reduce their payback periods to about five years or less, compared to the current payback periods of up to 11 years.

sections.label: Water savings and reduced bills
sections.summary: The project saves 0.4 million gallons per day and reduces the company's water bills by around $1.5 million annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: The project results in water savings of 0.4 million gallons per day and reduces the company’s water bills by around $1.5 million annually.

sections.label: Clause 4 amends section 20
sections.summary: Clause 4 of the Bill will amend section 20 to enable the WBT to be charged on water supplied by PWS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Specifically, clause 4 of the Bill will amend section 20 to enable the WBT to be charged on water supplied by PWS.

sections.label: WBT on private desalination plants
sections.summary: The WBT will apply to private desalination plants and large rainwater harvesters with tanks larger than 350 cubic metres.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: The WBT will be imposed on private desalination plants and large rainwater harvesters, defined as those with tank sizes larger than 350 cubic metres.

sections.label: WBT and WCT affected entities
sections.summary: The WBT and WCT are expected to mainly affect entities such as country clubs, golf courses and industrial premises with tanks larger than 350 cubic metres.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: With this calibrated approach, the WBT and WCT are expected to mainly affect entities, such as country clubs, golf courses and industrial premises with tank sizes larger than 350 cubic metres.

sections.label: Phased implementation of new charges
sections.summary: The charges are intended for early 2025, phased in two steps: 50% of prevailing WBT and WCT rates in 2025 and full rates in 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: In response to the concerns of PWS, we intend to impose the charges in early 2025, giving the affected parties more than a year, to give time for transition and to adjust to the changes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Furthermore, we will phase in the new charges in two steps, with 50% of the prevailing WBT and WCT rates in 2025 and the full prevailing rates to be imposed in 2026.

sections.label: Five-year time-bar for monetary claims
sections.summary: Clause 15 introduces a five-year time-bar for monetary claims for overpayments or erroneous payments, commencing 1 January 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Fourth, clause 15 introduces a five-year time-bar for monetary claims for overpayments or erroneous payments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: This provision aligns with time-bars in other pieces of legislation, such as the Goods and Services Tax Act 1993 and the Customs Act 1960, which minimise agencies’ legal risks from very dated claims.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: We intend to commence the time-bar from 1 January 2025, about one-and-a-half years from now.

sections.label: Minister may impose different WBT amounts
sections.summary: Section 20(4)(g) allows the Minister to impose different amounts of WBT for persons differently situated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Section 20(4)(g) allows the Minister to impose different amounts of WBT for persons "differently situated".

sections.label: PUB condition on water installation ownership
sections.summary: PUB may impose a condition requiring ownership of a water installation to be transferred to PUB when granting approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In granting approval for a water installation, PUB is allowed to impose a condition requiring ownership of any water installation to be transferred to PUB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State clarify if PUB will make payment to a person who transfers ownership of a water installation to PUB?

sections.label: WBT and WCT cost implications
sections.summary: Asks whether the WBT and WCT will have cost implications for SMEs and individual consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can I confirm that the WBT and WCT will not have any cost implications for the small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and individual consumers?

sections.label: Water demand and production cost
sections.summary: Asks whether growth in water demand raises average water production cost that may be passed to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Is the growth in water demand resulting in an increase in the average cost of water production which may be passed on to our Singaporeans?

sections.label: Recycling requirements in specific sectors
sections.summary: Notes recycling requirements cover wafer fabrication, electronics and biomed, which are one-fifth of the sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While it is commendable that we are implementing recycling requirements in specific sectors like wafer fabrication, electronics and biomed, we must consider the broader picture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: These sectors, though significant contributors to non-domestic water demand, represent only one-fifth of the entire sector.

sections.label: Wafer fabrication recycling target
sections.summary: Notes the proposed 50% wafer fabrication recycling target and that Taiwan has achieved 75%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The proposed target of achieving a 50% recycling rate for wafer fabrication is a commendable step.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, it is worth noting that Taiwan has already achieved a recycling rate of 75% in the same sector.

sections.label: Number of PWS in Singapore
sections.summary: Asks PUB to share the overall numbers of PWS operating in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can PUB share on the overall numbers of PWS operating in Singapore?

sections.label: PWS price increases and water security
sections.summary: Says PWS should not raise prices to offset new charges and welcomes the Bill on water demand and recycling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In particular, PWS should not be permitted to increase prices to offset the new charges as a result of these amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this high inflationary environment, essential public goods, such as water, must continue to remain accessible to our residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I welcome this Bill which seeks to manage Singapore's water demand, projected to almost double in 40 years' time and safeguard supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I support the introduction of mandatory water recycling requirements for industries which use huge quantities of water, as well as giving more legal powers to PUB to ensure our water security.

sections.label: WBT WCT impact on PWS
sections.summary: Asks whether imposing WBT and WCT would adversely impact PWS and discourage their services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would not the imposition of the WBT and WCT have an adverse impact on PWS, discouraging them from the provision of their services?

sections.label: Small rainwater harvester exemption threshold
sections.summary: States small rainwater harvesters below 350 cubic metres are exempted from WBT and WCT, and asks what considerations set this threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: All small rainwater harvesters, defined as below 350 cubic metres, will be exempted from both WBT and WCT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What were the considerations in deciding on this volume threshold?

sections.label: Recycling rate consultations with companies
sections.summary: After consultations with companies, a 50% recycling rate was found reasonable and doable, with existing plants at a 40% median.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: After consultations with companies, we found that a recycling rate of 50% would be reasonable and doable currently.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Today, the median recycling rate for existing wafer fabrication plants in Singapore is 40%, although some facilities are already recycling beyond 50%.

sections.label: UMC expansion plant recycling rate
sections.summary: UMC's expansion plant, scheduled for commissioning in 2024, is designed to achieve a recycling rate above 60%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: For example, United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC)'s expansion plant, which is scheduled to be commissioned in 2024, is designed to achieve a recycling rate of above 60%.

sections.label: WEF and IWSDF grant recipients
sections.summary: As of June 2023, 375 successful applicants received WEF and IWSDF grants ranging from $10,000 to $4 million per project.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: As of June 2023, 375 successful applicants have received grants under the WEF and IWSDF, with the grant amounts ranging from $10,000 to $4 million per project.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: When the projects are fully implemented, it would result in potential water savings of over 70 million litres a day.

sections.label: Raising water recycling rate benefits
sections.summary: Raising the water recycling rate contributes to sustainability in water demand growth and enhances Singapore's long-term water security.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Raising the water recycling rate will contribute to sustainability in water demand growth and enhance Singapore's water security in the long term.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Recycling beyond 50% will result in even greater water savings for the companies while placing Singapore in a better position to host more high-value water-intensive investments.

sections.label: PUB waiver of water efficiency requirements
sections.summary: Proposed section 40(8) lets PUB waive or modify prescribed water efficiency requirements when there are good reasons.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The proposed section 40(8), introduced by clause 12 of the Bill, is meant to address this.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: It empowers PUB to waive or modify any prescribed water efficiency requirement, if there are good reasons to do so.

sections.label: Number of PWS
sections.summary: There are currently around 300 PWS in total.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Currently, there are around 300 PWS in total.

sections.label: WBT for large rainwater harvesters
sections.summary: WBT applies only to rainwater harvesters with tanks above 350 cubic metres, capturing around 80% of privately harvested rainwater volume.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: As a practical and calibrated approach, we will impose the WBT only for large rainwater harvesters, whose tank sizes are greater than 350 cubic metres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This would capture harvesters who collectively harvest the majority, or around 80%, of the volume of all privately harvested rainwater.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This will allow us to strike a balance between the ideal policy position that WBT should be applied to all rainwater harvesters while helping the industry manage the administrative costs of compliance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Hence, to Mr Don Wee's suggestion on whether the charges would affect SMEs and individual consumers, I would want to say that those with tank sizes of 350 cubic metres and below will not be affected.

sections.label: Phased WBT implementation for PWS
sections.summary: PUB will implement the charges in early 2025 and adopt a phased approach to help PWS cope with the transition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To address Mr Gan's concerns and help PWS cope with the transition, PUB will only implement the charges in early 2025, instead of immediately, and adopt a phased approach to implement the charges, as I have said earlier in my opening speech.

sections.label: WBT rates for PWS
sections.summary: PWS will be charged the same WBT rates as PUB-supplied water for non-domestic premises, currently 92 cents per cubic metre.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The intention is to charge PWS the same WBT rates as PUB-supplied water for non-domestic premises, currently at 92 cents per cubic metre, and this will be specified in the subsidiary legislation.

sections.label: Entry into private premises
sections.summary: PUB will assess each case and ensure any entry into private premises is justified and proportionate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Regardless of which section applies, PUB will assess the situation in each case and ensure that any entry into private premises is justified and proportionate.

sections.label: Diversion plans and PUB ownership
sections.summary: Section 26 is amended to require developers to submit diversion plans to PUB, which then takes over ownership of the water installation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Section 26 will be amended to regularise the existing requirement for developers to submit diversion plans to PUB for approval before they start works to divert PUB’s pipes and water installation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: As such, after developers divert the water installation, PUB will take over the ownership of the water installation for long-term maintenance and operational flexibility without any payment or cost to the development.

sections.label: E-notices opt-in and Act relevance
sections.summary: The amendment makes e-notices an opt-in system, not an automatic replacement, and aims to keep the Act relevant for water security.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The amendment does not provide for e-notices to automatically replace hard copy notices.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This is an opt-in system for customers who prefer to receive e-notices in lieu of hard copies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The proposed amendments under this Bill serve to ensure that the Act remains relevant and effective in safeguarding our water security through sustainable water demand management and reliable supply of water, especially in light of climate change and increasing water demand.
